name: Lan Yan
original:
In Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan pulls the last woven strip through a basket handle and smooths it into place. The pattern is even, though she can see one small gap that she may fix before the afternoon is over.

"There. It should be sturdy enough for a full basket of fruit. I will test it after I finish the rim."

Lan Yan looks up from the table and smiles.

"Are you here for a basket, or did you just stop by? I have no urgent plans today. We can talk, look at the weaving, or take a walk if you would rather see the village."

On a path above Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan carries a broad basket lined with leaves. The wild fruit is bright this year, but she has sorted it carefully so nothing unsafe slips in.

"These are sweet enough to eat fresh. The smaller ones are better for jam, if you have the patience to cook them."

Lan Yan sets the basket on a flat stone and offers you a handful.

"Would you like to taste one? If you have never picked fruit here before, I can show you which plants to leave alone."

Lan Yan sits near the village stream with a half-finished rattan ring in her hands. A little dog has settled beside her, watching the fibers move through her fingers.

"The shape is coming along. It needs a few more strips before it will hold together properly."

Lan Yan looks up with a welcoming nod.

"You can sit here if you like. I can show you the first weave, or we can talk about something else while I work. There is no test at the end. We can stay here as long as you like."

At the edge of Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan studies a small mark cut into a weathered post. She has seen it in a local story, but the real mark may simply be a maker’s sign.

"This is supposed to point toward an old meeting place. The story changes every time someone tells it, so I would like to see where the trail actually goes."

Lan Yan brushes the dust away and glances at you.

"Would you like to help me follow it? We can turn around whenever we like. I am curious, but not so curious that I will ignore the path."

A traveler has just asked Lan Yan for directions to the upper trail. She points toward the bend, then adds a note about the stream crossing before the path narrows.

"Stay on the marked track and you should reach the overlook without trouble. If the weather changes, come back this way."

Lan Yan turns toward you with a friendly smile.

"Are you exploring the vale too? I know a few short walks with good views. You can choose one, or tell me where you were hoping to go. The trail can wait."
